stem.en: Kabir asks what the bands would show after three divisions. What does semi-conservative predict?

text.en: Two bands again: one halfway and one light, but now the light band is three times the size of the halfway one. The two original heavy strands are still there, each in a half-heavy helix, among six all-light helices.

feedback.en: There are only ever two kinds of helix after the first division: half-heavy, and light. The bands stay two; their sizes change.

text.en: One light band; the heavy is gone.

feedback.en: The original strands are never destroyed. They are still there, each paired with a light partner, forever.
Only the two helices holding original strands are halfway. Every other helix is light.

explanation.en: Count strands. Two original heavy strands exist, always. Every division doubles the helices, and all new strands are light.
